title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 95
paragraphs: The islanders furnished seventeen ships and were armed like Greeks; these too are a Pelasgian race, though they came later to be called Ionian by the same principle as the Ionians of the Twelve Cities, who came from Athens. The Aeolians supplied sixty ships; they were equipped like Greeks and used in old times to be called Pelasgians, as the Greeks report. The people of the Hellespont — except those of Abydus (for the men of Abydus had been appointed by the king to stay in place and guard the bridges) — the rest of those who served in the expedition from the Pontic region furnished a hundred ships and were equipped like Greeks. These are colonists of the Ionians and Dorians.
